question.text: A first-time sponsor, Mr. Kiran Joshi, is applying to SEBI for AIF registration. Which of the following is a mandatory eligibility requirement applicable to the Sponsor?

answer.text: Must be a person/entity satisfying 'fit and proper' criteria specified in Schedule II of the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008; and must be responsible for formation & registration of the AIF
Must be a listed entity with market cap exceeding INR 1000 crore
Must have personally managed at least INR 500 crore in a regulated AMC for 10 years
Must be an SEBI-registered Merchant Banker in its own right

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, the Sponsor must satisfy the fit and proper person criteria specified in Schedule II of the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008. 'Sponsor' is defined as any person or entity responsible for formation and registration of the AIF with SEBI; includes promoter in case of a company and designated partner in case of LLP. Sponsors can be any person or persons including institutions or companies. **The Trap:** The market-cap distractor invents a requirement. The AUM-track-record distractor invents a rule (not applicable to sponsor per se — track record is relevant to Manager qualification). The MB-in-its-own-right distractor confuses Sponsor with Merchant Banker. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C covers the same fit-and-proper standard. III-A/III-C (Compliance) tests Schedule II of SEBI Intermediaries Regulations in detail. Note: Sponsor's 'fit and proper' is DIFFERENT from Manager's registration requirements — Sponsor can be an individual with no AMC history. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Schedule II covers integrity, reputation, financial soundness and absence of convictions — maintain clean personal/entity records. Any pending regulatory proceedings (even unrelated sectors) are disclosed in the SEBI registration application and can delay approval by 3-6 months.
